title: Collider taxonomy — how colliders are classified — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "Collider taxonomy — how colliders are classified". The classification axes and machine facts belong to the public record. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: the taxonomy itself is a decision tool. Given a physics question, the axes pick the machine: need new particles? maximize centre-of-mass energy (hadron ring). Need precision couplings? maximize luminosity at the right resonance with the cleanest initial state (lepton factory). Need nuclear matter? heavy ions. The Signature completion turns the taxonomy into a worked decision procedure with public examples: the Higgs needed a hadron discovery machine first (LHC) and will want a lepton Higgs factory next (FCC-ee/ILC/CEPC) — the field's actual strategy, organized as a reusable method.

title: Tevatron — Fermilab's proton-antiproton collider — Signature layer

Signature analysis: the Tevatron is the case study in technology transition — the first superconducting-magnet collider, built when that technology was a gamble, which then became the assumed foundation for everything after. The Signature completion studies the gamble: what evidence justified scaling superconductors to kilometres in the 1980s, what the failure modes were, and how the successful run de-risked the LHC's far larger bet. The joint CDF/D0 top discovery is treated as the template for independent-confirmation culture.

title: RHIC — the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "RHIC — the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider". The machine facts, the perfect-liquid discovery, and the spin program belong to the public record. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: RHIC is the case study in versatility as strategy — one ring, many species, polarized beams — versus the LHC's single-species optimization. The Signature completion compares the two strategies' payoffs: RHIC's flexibility produced the spin puzzle and the liquid discovery from the same machine; the LHC's focus produced the Higgs. Neither strategy dominates; the lesson is portfolio design across a field, not within one machine. The tunnel's planned handoff to the EIC continues the reuse pattern.

title: LEP — the Large Electron-Positron Collider — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "LEP — the Large Electron-Positron Collider". The precision program, the neutrino-family count, and the synchrotron wall belong to the public record. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: LEP is the purest demonstration that precision is discovery — no new particle was found at LEP, yet its measurements predicted the top quark's mass and cornered the Higgs. The Signature completion works through the logic of indirect discovery: when theory relates measurable quantities to unknown masses (radiative corrections), measuring the known precisely reveals the unknown approximately. That logic now drives the entire Higgs-factory case for FCC-ee/ILC/CEPC.

Concept layer (labeled): a Signature-organized "indirect discovery ledger" — public cases where precision predicted particles before direct observation (top quark, W/Z masses, Higgs mass range) — as an educational pattern, not new physics.

Work LEP's predictions as the precision-discovers pattern
Organize a labeled ledger of indirect-discovery cases
Connect the logic to the Higgs-factory proposals
Keep LEP facts public, methodology here

title: SLC — the Stanford Linear Collider — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "SLC — the Stanford Linear Collider". The linear design, polarization, and SLD facts belong to the public record. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: the SLC is the case study in proof-of-principle machines — it never competed with LEP on statistics, yet it proved linear colliders work and that polarization multiplies physics per collision. The Signature completion generalizes the lesson: a small, clever machine can de-risk a whole future direction. The polarization story is worked as a force-multiplier pattern: an 80-percent-polarized beam gave a 600,000-Z machine measurements that stood beside a 17-million-Z machine's.

title: B-factories — KEKB, PEP-II, and the matter-antimatter asymmetry — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "B-factories — KEKB, PEP-II, and the matter-antimatter asymmetry". The factory strategy, the 2001 CP-violation result, and the Nobel belong to the public record. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: the B-factories are the case study in the second strategy — when energy can't go higher, go brighter — and in independent confirmation as culture: Belle and BaBar raced to the same measurement and published together. The Signature completion works through the "sharpened mystery" outcome: the Standard Model's CP violation confirmed but insufficient for the universe's matter content, which is a productive failure — it tells the field exactly where to look next (leptonic CP violation, electric dipole moments).

Concept layer (labeled): a Signature "productive failure" taxonomy — results that close one door while pointing at the next — offered as an organizing view, not physics.

title: Future colliders — FCC, ILC, CLIC, CEPC, muon collider, EIC — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "Future colliders — FCC, ILC, CLIC, CEPC, muon collider, EIC". The proposal parameters and statuses belong to the public record. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: the future-collider portfolio is a decision problem under uncertainty, and the Signature completion works it as one: each proposal is scored on physics reach, technical readiness, cost scale, and timeline, using only public design-report figures. No winner is picked — the analysis instead shows the trade structure: circular proton machines maximize energy, linear electron machines maximize cleanliness, muon machines maximize energy-per-kilometre but carry the highest technical risk, and the EIC is already being built because its risk is lowest.

Concept layer (labeled): a Signature decision-matrix template for comparing proposed megaprojects, offered as a planning tool. The standing rule is enforced: proposals are proposals; nothing here claims any machine will be built.

title: Collider records table — energies, luminosities, eras — Signature layer
body:
This Signature-layer record mirrors the public record "Collider records table — energies, luminosities, eras". The table values and the Livingston plot belong to the public record. This layer adds original Signature analysis.

Signature analysis: the Livingston plot is really a plot of sustained institutional will — a century of roughly tenfold energy gains per decade, each step requiring a new technology when the old one walled out. The Signature completion reads the plot's slope changes as technology S-curves: electrostatic, cyclotron, synchrotron, superconducting, and now the question of what bends the curve next (plasma wakefield? muons?). The completion also notes the plot's hidden variable: cost per unit energy has stayed roughly flat only because each technology was cheaper per GeV than the last — when that stops, the plot stops.

Concept layer (labeled): a Signature "curve-bending watchlist" of public R&D directions that could restart steep gains, organized as a watchlist, not a forecast.
capabilities: Read the Livingston plot as technology S-curves
Explain the hidden cost-per-GeV variable
Maintain a labeled curve-bending watchlist
Show where each technology walled out
Keep table values public, curve analysis here

# S-curves behind the Livingston plot (Signature reading)

          ("superconducting", "1980s-now", "walled by field limits"),
          ("plasma/muon ?", "R&D", "unproven at scale")]
